intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Crittenden County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: During our evaluation, nothing came to our attention that would warrant disclosure in this report.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated December 18, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Gilmore
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor, Recorder/Treasurer, and District Court Clerk. Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer Schedule 1 of this report shows a General Fund balance of $653. It was brought to our attention that as of December 31, 2024, the General Fund owed a significant amount to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DFA) for taxes owed as well as balances due to the Street and Fire Equipment and Training Funds. As shown in Note 5 on Schedule 3, when these outstanding amounts were considered, the General Fund had a deficit balance of $54,257.

cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and City Clerk.
